title: Newsmax Posts First Profit Streak as Q3 Revenue Tops Estimates, Shares Climb 14%
text:

 Add preferred source Newsmax Inc. (NYSE:NMAX) reported third-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings of 12 cents per share, beating a 1-cent loss estimate, as revenue rose 52.5% to $69.03 million, above the $49.83 million consensus. Excluding a $14 million one-time termination payment, revenue grew 21.6% to a record $55 million. Affiliate fees climbed 77.4% and licensing revenue jumped 291%, while digital revenue slipped 4.1%. Adjusted EBITDA reached $19 million versus a year-earlier loss, and net income of $15.2 million reversed a prior loss. Shares rose 14%. The company reaffirmed 2026 revenue guidance of $212 million to $216 million and cited its Meta Platforms partnership and AI licensing as growth areas. Key Elements 
 Newsmax Inc. Christopher Ruddy Meta Platforms Inc. Newsmax+ NYSE:NMAX NASDAQ:META Newsmax Inc. (NYSE:NMAX) reported third-quarter 2026 results that beat Wall Street estimates on both lines, sending shares up 14% and marking the conservative media company's strongest quarter since its listing.
 Adjusted earnings came in at 12 cents per share, well ahead of the 1-cent loss analysts had projected. Revenue for the quarter ended Sept. 30 totaled $69.03 million, up 52.5% from $45.3 million a year earlier and above the $49.83 million consensus. The top line included a $14 million one-time service revenue termination payment; excluding that item, revenue rose 21.6% to a record $55 million.
 "The third quarter was the strongest in our history as a public company," Chief Executive Christopher Ruddy said. "Setting aside the one-time revenue item, we delivered our fastest revenue growth since our listing and a second consecutive profitable quarter."
 Affiliate fees did much of the heavy lifting, climbing 77.4% to $14.3 million, while licensing revenue jumped 291% to $4.7 million. Broadcasting advertising revenue edged up 3.1% to $24.3 million. Total broadcasting revenue rose 65.9% to $60.7 million, or 27.6% to $46.7 million excluding the one-time payment, helped by new contracts, rate increases and international licensing agreements.
 Digital was the weak spot: revenue fell 4.1% to $8.3 million as lower subscription and product sales and softer digital advertising outweighed gains from media and AI licensing.
 Profitability swung sharply positive. Adjusted EBITDA reached $19 million, compared with a $900,000 loss a year earlier; excluding the one-time item, it was $5 million. Net income totaled $15.2 million, or 12 cents per share, reversing a year-earlier loss of $4.1 million, or 3 cents per share.

 Cash and short-term investments $137.6M — — 
 Note: The company reported no debt at quarter-end. Adjusted EBITDA excluding the $14 million one-time termination fee was $5.0 million.
 On the audience side, Newsmax said it reached 22.5 million viewers during the quarter, including 9.1 million adults aged 35 to 64. Social media followers rose 13% to 26.8 million as of Sept. 30, and the Newsmax+ streaming service expanded its library past 700 documentaries and specials. Ruddy pointed to rising engagement during the midterm election campaign as a trend that could support growth into the 2028 presidential race.
 Management reaffirmed underlying 2026 revenue guidance of $212 million to $216 million, implying about 13% growth at the $214 million midpoint, and said it expects roughly $16 million in international licensing revenue this year, up 344%. Including the one-time payment, full-year revenue is projected at $226 million to $230 million. The company also flagged its multiyear partnership with Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) and sees further opportunities in AI content licensing, while planning to trim spending on legacy publications in favor of streaming, digital distribution and international licensing.
 The swing to a second straight profitable quarter gives Newsmax a firmer financial footing as it diversifies beyond cable carriage, though the digital decline and reliance on affiliate-fee growth will be watched closely by investors gauging whether the momentum can carry into 2027.
